A kept entry names the kinds of influence its sentence states, a one-line summary in the atlas voice, and whether the tie ended or met protest. A drop says why. Candidates not listed here are not reviewed yet and are not shown. check "record" means checked against the record text, not yet against the source page. Batch 3 (17 Nov 2026): Sony Pictures Entertainment at LACMA, the one tie where a record links a funder’s lobbying and political giving to a space (entries may carry links: [{measure, text, source}]). Batch 4 (17 Nov 2026): BP at the British Museum, the Days of the Dead evening (2015) and the Scythians breakfast (2017); measure 'other' is lobbying of a government outside the US and the EU, named in `gov`. Batch 5 (17 Nov 2026): BP and UK ministers at the Science Museum, British Museum and National Portrait Gallery (2015, Art Not Oil FOI releases); Philip Morris at the Met and BAM against the 1994 Vallone bill (Truth Tobacco Industry Documents). Batch 6 (17 Nov 2026): UK government hospitality returns naming BP or Bloomberg as host at a space (British Museum, Royal Opera House, National Portrait Gallery, Serpentine, Tate Britain): hospitality, not the subject of any request. Batch 7 (17 Nov 2026): the Commons Register of Members' Financial Interests (via TheyWorkForYou's copy), BP at the Royal Opera House and JTI at the British Museum and the Royal Academy: hospitality to MPs at a space. Batch 8 (17 Nov 2026): two new spaces, Opera Queensland and Queensland Museum, with Queensland ministerial diary entries (Rio Tinto 2013; Shell and its QGC business 2018, 2019) and Shell QGC's $10.25 million to the museum since 2015.
